target: Let V be convex in a real normed space E with its original norm. Let A(x)=psi(x)+sum_(i<n)loss_i(x), and G(x)=psi(x)+sum_(i<n+1)loss_i(x)+indicator_V(x). Each included loss excludes bottom globally and is finite on V. Suppose the actual total G has lambda-strong curvature on V, lambda>=0, p belongs to V and minimizes A+hint on V. Let the continuous functional g support loss_n-hint at p on V. Then for every q in V, G(p)-G(q)<=g(p-q)-(lambda/2)||p-q||^2. Feasible values are proved finite internally before using toReal. This is the sharp local stability implication in the finite common-domain branch of Lemma7.5 and Theorem7.47, not either complete numbered result. Source Algorithm7.8 only requires the played point to lie in the current loss domain; common finiteness on V is an explicit branch qualification. Algorithm15.9 already prints the common-domain condition. Local continuous-dual support is weaker than source global coordinate subgradient membership; only the global-to-local implication is intended. The ambient arbitrary real normed space generalizes the source finite-dimensional conditional inequality; no finite-dimensional attainment claim follows. The header assumes total-objective curvature, not regularizer-only curvature. n=0, lambda=0 and nonzero g are allowed. The actual prediction minimum supplies p, not a hidden minimum of G. No closedness, support-existence or attainment conclusion is supplied.

old.lean_notes: Two kernel-checked experimental canaries use E=R^2 with the sup norm, V=[-1,1]^2, f(x)=(x0^2+x1^2)/2+x0 on V and top outside, p=0 and q=(1,1). For ordinary coordinates and g=(1,0), the chosen squared norm is1 and coordinate Euclidean squared norm is2; the correct bound is3/2<=2, while a wrong Euclidean penalty still gives2<=2, so this first numerical bound alone cannot detect that error. Scaling coordinates to e prime=2e and g prime=g/2 preserves pairing1 and the E penalty1/2, while the coordinate squared norm becomes8. The wrong substituted penalty would give5<=2, which the second canary explicitly refutes.
